projection: Dates after the last published quarter use the last published rate; dates before the first entry use the first. The percentages and the $150,000/$75,000 AGI thresholds are statutory and not inflation-indexed.

content.note: Figures were checked on October 9, 2026 against the IRS quarterly interest rate page, the Internal Revenue Bulletins it links, the IRS news releases and the statute. The engine module docstring maps these rules to engine fields.

content.value: Lesser of 90% of the current year's tax or 100% of the prior year's tax
110% when prior-year AGI exceeds $150,000 ($75,000 married filing separately). Not inflation-indexed
25% of the required annual payment each
April 15, June 15 and September 15 of the tax year; January 15 of the next year
From each due date to the earlier of April 15 of the next year or the date paid
Payments are credited against unpaid installments in due-date order
Deemed paid in equal parts on each due date
No addition when the tax shown, less withholding, is under $1,000
No addition when the prior year was a 12-month year with no tax liability and the individual was a citizen or resident all year
Chapter 1 tax (income tax, including AMT and the §72(t) additional tax), chapter 2 (self-employment tax), chapter 2A (net investment income tax), less part IV credits other than withholding
The §3101(b)(2) tax not withheld counts as chapter 2 tax
The §6621(a)(2) underpayment rate: federal short-term rate plus 3 percentage points, set quarterly

content: Dates after the last published quarter use the last published rate (7%). Dates before 2024 use the first row.
Interest is simple, computed per day with 365 or 366 days in each calendar year. §6622 daily compounding does not apply to the §6654 addition.
Due dates are the statutory dates. Weekend and holiday shifts (§7503) are not applied.

Not modeled: state estimated-tax penalties, the annualized income installment method (Form 2210 Schedule AI), waivers (§6654(e)(3)), farmer and fisher rules, interest or failure-to-pay penalties after April 15, and interest on refunds.
